key_insight: A training-free, non-generative readout classified ASA physical status about 64× faster than rationale-generating prompting, while calibration with a few hundred local labels brought agreement close to LoRA fine-tuning.
clinical_relevance: This approach could reduce computational and site-specific adapter maintenance burdens for ASA classification, but the reported agreement does not establish human-level performance or clinical readiness.
method: Compared generative zero-shot prompting, non-generative readout, locally calibrated readout and LoRA using Qwen3.5-9B.
Used structured preoperative variables, with or without diagnosis text, to classify ASA I, II, III and IV–V.
Evaluated quadratic-weighted kappa, speed and label requirements against recorded ASA classes.
evidence_signal: The retrospective study used MOVER (57,473 operations), local temporal validation (2,753) and VitalDB (6,242); local-validation kappa was 0.460 for the readout versus 0.227 for rationale-generating zero-shot prompting.
watch_item: Non-inferiority to LoRA was conditional and borderline in stricter sensitivity analyses; LoRA retained higher kappa with more labels and higher exact agreement.
paper_title: Non-generative readout with few-label calibration versus LoRA fine-tuning of a large language model for ASA physical status classification: accuracy, speed, cost and label efficiency in three data sources
